title: TEACHING EXAMPLE: one of two miniature frontier-shaped instances, depth over breadth
note: Teaching example, not part of the benchmark. It mirrors the shape of the scored frontier_swe_hard cards (small sealed instance list, threshold well below the instance count, PASS_TO_PASS regressions that punish shallow fixes) at miniature scale so it grades in about a second with no docker and no network. The scored cards run the pinned swebench docker harness over SWE-bench Verified instances rated 1 to 4+ hours of human effort; this card uses examples/frontier_swe_hard/assets/mini_harness.py, a stand-in, not SWE-bench. Reference solution: examples/frontier_swe_hard/solution/.
goal: Finish with at least one of the two sealed instances in assets/ex-frontier_swe_hard/instances.txt resolved. Both are deeper than the swe_bench demo: demoorg__tinygraph-201 needs a coordinated edit across three files (a new exception type, its export, and the raise site), and demoorg__tinyunits-202 has a shallow patch that satisfies the reported symptom while breaking an existing invariant. Triage both instances first, then go deep on the ones you pick rather than spraying one-line patches: an instance counts as resolved only when every sealed FAIL_TO_PASS test passes AND every sealed PASS_TO_PASS test still passes, and the sealed tests are copied over your patched tree after the patch applies. Write one JSON object per attempted instance to runs/ex-frontier_swe_hard/predictions.jsonl with keys instance_id, model_name_or_path set exactly to 'ex-frontier_swe_hard', and model_patch (a git-apply-able diff with a/ and b/ prefixes, rooted at the instance repo). Record every intermediate harness verdict, name the cause of every unresolved instance, and re-plan explicitly after each red round while budget remains.
resources: pypi: pytest (any recent version; the demo harness shells out to python3 -m pytest)
assets/ex-frontier_swe_hard/instances.txt (sealed instance-id list, one id per line)

output convention: runs/ex-frontier_swe_hard/predictions.jsonl with model_name_or_path set exactly to 'ex-frontier_swe_hard', so the harness report is written to ex-frontier_swe_hard.<run_id>.json in the workspace root

spec.command: python3 assets/ex-frontier_swe_hard/mini_harness.py --predictions runs/ex-frontier_swe_hard/predictions.jsonl --instances-dir assets/ex-frontier_swe_hard/instances --instance-ids-file assets/ex-frontier_swe_hard/instances.txt --work-dir work/ex-frontier_swe_hard/harness --report-dir . --run-id ex-frontier_swe_hard && python3 -c "import json; r=json.load(open('ex-frontier_swe_hard.ex-frontier_swe_hard.json')); print(json.dumps({'resolved_instances': r['resolved_instances']}))"

process_expectations: A plan artifact exists at runs/ex-frontier_swe_hard/plan.md before the first patch attempt, naming the target instance ids, the suspected fault location in each, and the exact verification command.
Triage before depth: the plan records why each instance was chosen as a primary target or deferred, not just which one was patched.
Verification actually ran: at least one harness execution on candidate patches before the final grading run, with its verdict recorded.
Failure identities are tracked: runs/ex-frontier_swe_hard/failures.md lists each unresolved instance id with a one-line cause (the failing test id or the patch-apply error), not just counts.
Honest cost and attempt logging: runs/ex-frontier_swe_hard/ledger.json records per-attempt spend and outcome, including failed and abandoned attempts.
Recovery after RED: if a harness run misses the threshold, artifacts show a revised plan and a re-run rather than a silent stop.
No test-shaped shortcuts: the diff must fix the reported behaviour in the source tree, not special-case the values the reported symptom mentions.
